back_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. The attached image is the exact design target. Make ONE reverse-camera view of the SAME RIGHT human hand wearing the SAME fitted brown leather glove and short forearm, as a second image-to-3D reference. Rotate the camera around the upright subject by 180 degrees to show the dorsal BACK of the hand in a mild 15-degree three-quarter view. Do NOT mirror the object, change it to a left hand, create a second subject, or alter the neutral pose, scale, digit lengths, thumb abduction/opposition, palm thickness, wrist width, short forearm length, brown material or overall silhouette. Fingers still point up, proximal forearm down. In this back view the SAME right-hand thumb is on the viewer's LEFT, the little finger on the RIGHT; show four knuckles and the subtle extensor forms naturally under fitted leather. Keep middle finger longest; thumb rounded and palmward with believable root volume. Thin dark-brown stitch panels, subtle leather grain, no deep baggy wrinkles. Same white background, same image framing/margins, soft even studio lighting and neutral material colour. Solid worn-hand exterior, leather continues smoothly onto a short tapering forearm with a simple truncated proximal end. No empty cuff cavity, rolled edge, flared lip, internal lining, exposed skin, armor, weapon, text, inset, dimensions, second view or duplicate hand. Preserve the camera-independent geometry; only camera and visible dorsal panels should change.
scope: Reverse view guidance; identity/geometry consistency remains a 3D validation requirement
